_meta.cn_source: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Soil Conservation Service (1986). Urban hydrology for small watersheds (TR-55), Table 2-2
_meta.soil_source: Rawls et al. (1993), as cited in Texas Department of Transportation (n.d.), Hydraulic Design Manual, Table 4-27 (inches converted to mm)
_meta.note: Eq 14 uses E_d = 24 * ks_mm_hr (mm/day). Proposal Section 5.2 used Rawls et al. (1983) via Chow et al. (1988) in cm/h; update that section if this set is kept.

gravel_or_dirt.ks_default_status: project-defined midpoint of the cited range; test the range in the sensitivity analysis

partial_pavement.status: project-defined; CN computed by Eq 4 (79.5 with these values)

full_pavement.ks_source: InfoWorks ICM (n.d.), SWMM runoff model: impervious surfaces modeled as 100% runoff after initial loss [verify year]
full_pavement.initial_abstraction_source: Wastewater Planning Users Group, User Note No. 28, cross-check against the ~1.0 mm derived from CN 98 [verify year]
full_pavement.depression_storage_source: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (2009), SWMM applications manual (EPA/600/R-09/000): about 0.05 in typical for impervious surfaces, traced to the USACE STORM model [verify page]
full_pavement.depression_storage_range_source: SWMM reported range, cited in a depression-storage study [verify which study before citing]
full_pavement.depression_storage_measured_source: Nehls et al. (2015), laser scanning of 11 pavement designs [verify full citation]
full_pavement.depression_storage_status: reference only; this is how much water pavement holds before runoff starts, not how fast it drains, so it is NOT used as drainage_mm_day
full_pavement.storm_drain_design_source: Federal Highway Administration, HEC-22, 4th ed. (minor storm drain systems) [verify year]
full_pavement.mannings_n_source: Delaware DOT drainage manual [verify title and year]
full_pavement.drainage_status: no sourced value; pavement drains through gutters and storm drains sized by design storm, not by a per-surface rate; full pavement flood duration not modeled (listed as limitation)
full_pavement.runoff_coefficient_source: American Society of Civil Engineers (1992), cross-check only [verify original page]
